Bilgoraj Oldest Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Biłgoraj, Poland

Demolished. Biłgoraj's most notable Jewish family, the Zilbermans, served as local rabbis from the 1880s through the interwar period — ancestors of the Nobel Prize-winning writer Isaac Bashevis Singer. This, the town's oldest Jewish cemetery, was likely established shortly after Biłgoraj's founding in 1578, with interwar reports noting tombstones as old as the 16th century; it remained in use until around 1730, when a second cemetery took over. By 1939, the Jewish community had grown to 60 percent of the town's population, before Germans destroyed the entire synagogue complex during WWII and deported the ghetto's residents to the Bełżec extermination camp in 1942, murdering several hundred more on the spot. No tombstones from this cemetery have ever been recovered; apartment blocks and garages now occupy the site, marked only by a boulder monument.
